seo.title: DiscVault — a catalogue for your discs
seo.description: DiscVault catalogues the films you own on 4K, Blu-ray and DVD. Scan a barcode, keep editions straight, on your device or your own server. No tracking.

leader.lead: DiscVault catalogues the films you own — on disc, on your shelf, on your own server.

shelf.lead: Browse posters, switch to list or detail views, filter by format, open box sets and containers. Fast on large collections.

read.lead: Scan a barcode and DiscVault fills in title, year, format and cover art. Or search by name.
read.captureAlt: DiscVault on iPhone: adding a movie after scanning its barcode

edition.lead: A 4K disc is not a Blu-ray. A steelbook is not a keepcase. Box sets, containers and the discs inside a release are catalogued as what they are.

vault.lead: On your device, or on a server you run. No analytics, no advertising, nobody watching what you watch.
body: The iPhone and iPad app keeps your collection on the device. DiscVault 26 keeps it on a server you administer. Either way the only thing that leaves is a barcode or a search term.

formats.lead: Self-hosted DiscVault 26 today. iPhone and iPad standalone. Android in beta.

routes.title: Self-hosted
body: A desktop-first library, richer detail pages, PostgreSQL foundations, plugins, migration tools and admin controls for collectors who keep their catalogue on their own server.
Invite-only flows, owner and admin tools, role-based access, audit views, API access and MCP-ready integrations.

routes.title: iPhone & iPad
body: Runs entirely on the device. Scan, enrich, filter and search without a server.

routes.title: Android
body: Request access on Discord. Approved testers install through Google Play.

formats.roadmap: The iOS and Android apps work standalone today. Connecting them to a self-hosted DiscVault installation is planned for a later stage.
